claim: Every DNA segment in a eukaryotic genome normally replicates once and only once per cell cycle to maintain genome stability.
source: Every DNA segment in a eukaryotic genome normally replicates once and only once per cell cycle to maintain genome stability.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about DNA replication control in eukaryotes.

claim: Alternative transposition during S phase can induce re-replication of transposable elements and their flanking sequences.
source: Our results suggest that alternative transposition during S phase can induce re-replication of the TEs and their flanking sequences.
evidence: The manuscript presents experimental results showing this phenomenon.

claim: DNA re-replication can spontaneously abort to generate double-strand breaks.
source: The DNA re-replication can spontaneously abort to generate double-strand breaks, which can be repaired to generate Composite Insertions composed of transposon termini flanking segmental duplications of various lengths.
evidence: This is inferred from the observed structures of the Composite Insertions.

claim: Double-strand breaks from aborted re-replication can be repaired to generate Composite Insertions composed of transposon termini flanking segmental duplications of various lengths.
source: The DNA re-replication can spontaneously abort to generate double-strand breaks, which can be repaired to generate Composite Insertions composed of transposon termini flanking segmental duplications of various lengths.
evidence: The manuscript presents sequenced structures of multiple Composite Insertions.

claim: Alternative transposition coupled with DNA replication and repair can significantly alter genome structure.
source: These results show how alternative transposition coupled with DNA replication and repair can significantly alter genome structure and may have contributed to rapid genome evolution in maize and possibly other eukaryotes.
evidence: This is inferred from the observed genomic rearrangements.

claim: Alternative transposition may have contributed to rapid genome evolution in maize and possibly other eukaryotes.
source: These results show how alternative transposition coupled with DNA replication and repair can significantly alter genome structure and may have contributed to rapid genome evolution in maize and possibly other eukaryotes.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the observed mechanisms.

claim: Initiation of DNA replication in eukaryotic cells is controlled by the replication licensing system.
source: Initiation of DNA replication in eukaryotic cells is controlled by the replication licensing system (Blow, 1993; Blow and Dutta, 2005; Truong and Wu, 2011), which ensures that each segment of the genome is replicated only once per cell cycle.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The replication licensing system ensures that each segment of the genome is replicated only once per cell cycle.
source: Initiation of DNA replication in eukaryotic cells is controlled by the replication licensing system (Blow, 1993; Blow and Dutta, 2005; Truong and Wu, 2011), which ensures that each segment of the genome is replicated only once per cell cycle.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Misexpression or mutation of replication licensing factors can lead to DNA re-replication, genome instability, major chromosomal rearrangements, and tumorigenesis.
source: The expression and activity of the replication licensing factors are precisely regulated, and misexpression or mutation of these factors can lead to DNA re-replication, genome instability, major chromosomal rearrangements, and tumorigenesis (Melixetian et al., 2004; Green and Li, 2005; Rice et al., 2005; Hook et al., 2007; Liontos et al., 2007; Sugimoto et al., 2009; Green et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Misregulation of some histone methyltransferases can result in DNA re-replication in plants and animals.
source: Misregulation of some histone methyltransferases can also result in DNA re-replication in plants and animals (Jacob et al., 2010; Tardat et al., 2010; Fu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Some Class II DNA transposons, including the maize Ac/Ds system, E. coli TN10, and E. coli TN7, are known to transpose during DNA replication.
source: For example, some Class II DNA transposons, including the maize Ac/Ds system, E. coli TN10, and E. coli TN7, are known to transpose during DNA replication (Roberts et al., 1985; Chen et al., 1987; Peters and Craig, 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: If a replicated transposon excises and reinserts into an unreplicated site, the transposon can undergo one additional replication in the same S phase.
source: If a replicated transposon excises and reinserts into an unreplicated site, the transposon can undergo one additional replication in the same S phase; the re-replication, however, is limited to the TE itself and does not extend into the TE-flanking regions.
evidence: This is inferred from known transposon behavior during replication.

claim: In standard transposon re-replication, the re-replication is limited to the TE itself and does not extend into the TE-flanking regions.
source: If a replicated transposon excises and reinserts into an unreplicated site, the transposon can undergo one additional replication in the same S phase; the re-replication, however, is limited to the TE itself and does not extend into the TE-flanking regions.
evidence: This is inferred from known transposon behavior during replication.

claim: A pair of Ac termini in reversed orientation can undergo transposition, generating major chromosomal rearrangements such as deletions, inversions, permutations, duplications, and reciprocal translocations.
source: We and others have previously shown that a pair of Ac termini in reversed orientation can undergo transposition, generating major chromosomal rearrangements such as deletions, inversions, permutations, duplications, and reciprocal translocations (Zhang and Peterson, 2004; Zhang et al., 2006; Huang and Dooner, 2008; Zhang et al., 2009, 2013); this transposition reaction is termed reversed Ac ends transposition (RET).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research by the authors and others.

claim: The transposition reaction involving a pair of Ac termini in reversed orientation is termed reversed Ac ends transposition (RET).
source: We and others have previously shown that a pair of Ac termini in reversed orientation can undergo transposition, generating major chromosomal rearrangements such as deletions, inversions, permutations, duplications, and reciprocal translocations (Zhang and Peterson, 2004; Zhang et al., 2006; Huang and Dooner, 2008; Zhang et al., 2009, 2013); this transposition reaction is termed reversed Ac ends transposition (RET).
evidence: This is a definition provided in the text.

claim: All RET-generated genome rearrangements described to date are fully explained by models in which the excised TE termini inserted into target sites that had completed DNA replication.
source: All the RET-generated genome rearrangements described to date are fully explained by models in which the excised TE termini inserted into target sites that had completed DNA replication.
evidence: This is based on prior research and models.

claim: RET, like standard Ac/Ds transposition, may also occur during DNA replication.
source: However, it seems reasonable to expect that RET, like standard Ac/Ds transposition, may also occur during DNA replication, and that the excised reversed Ac termini could insert into unreplicated target sites.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on known transposon behavior.

claim: Excised reversed Ac termini could insert into unreplicated target sites.
source: However, it seems reasonable to expect that RET, like standard Ac/Ds transposition, may also occur during DNA replication, and that the excised reversed Ac termini could insert into unreplicated target sites.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on known transposon behavior.

claim: RET events with insertion into unreplicated target sites can induce re-replication of the TE and its flanking sequences.
source: Here, we show that such events do occur, and that they can induce re-replication of the TE and its flanking sequences.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: RET-induced re-replication generates novel structures termed Composite Insertions (CIs) that contain TE sequences and variable lengths of the flanking genomic DNA.
source: This process generates novel structures termed Composite Insertions (CIs) that contain TE sequences and variable lengths of the flanking genomic DNA.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: The allele P1-ovov454 carries an intact Ac element and a fractured Ac (fAc) element inserted in the second intron of the maize p1 gene.
source: The allele P1-ovov454 (GenBank accession # KM013692) carries an intact Ac element and a fractured Ac (fAc) element inserted in the second intron of the maize p1 gene; the 5′ terminus of Ac and the 3′ terminus of fAc are present in reversed orientation with respect to each other and separated by an 822-bp inter-transposon segment (Figure 1A) (Yu et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation and reference to Figure 1A.

claim: In P1-ovov454, the 5′ terminus of Ac and the 3′ terminus of fAc are present in reversed orientation with respect to each other and separated by an 822-bp inter-transposon segment.
source: The allele P1-ovov454 (GenBank accession # KM013692) carries an intact Ac element and a fractured Ac (fAc) element inserted in the second intron of the maize p1 gene; the 5′ terminus of Ac and the 3′ terminus of fAc are present in reversed orientation with respect to each other and separated by an 822-bp inter-transposon segment (Figure 1A) (Yu et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation and reference to Figure 1A.

claim: The P1-ovov454 allele undergoes RET to generate derivative alleles containing either deletions or Tandem Direct Duplications (TDDs).
source: Our recent work showed that the P1-ovov454 allele undergoes RET to generate derivative alleles containing either deletions or Tandem Direct Duplications (TDDs; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by prior research and reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Deletions and TDDs from P1-ovov454 are formed as a direct consequence of transposition of the Ac/fAc termini into a replicated target site on the sister chromatid.
source: These are formed as a direct consequence of transposition of the Ac/fAc termini into a replicated target site on the sister chromatid (Zhang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: The deletions and TDDs from P1-ovov454 vary in size depending on the position of the insertion site.
source: The deletions and TDDs vary in size depending on the position of the insertion site (green/black triangle in Figure 1—figure supplement 1); the TDDs previously characterized range in size from 8 kb to 5.3 Mb (Zhang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation and reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The TDDs previously characterized from P1-ovov454 range in size from 8 kb to 5.3 Mb.
source: The deletions and TDDs vary in size depending on the position of the insertion site (green/black triangle in Figure 1—figure supplement 1); the TDDs previously characterized range in size from 8 kb to 5.3 Mb (Zhang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Insertion of the Ac/fAc termini into the target site generates an 8-bp target site duplication (TSD).
source: Like standard Ac/Ds transposition, insertion of the Ac/fAc termini into the target site generates an 8-bp target site duplication (TSD; green/black triangle).
evidence: This is based on known transposon behavior and observed in the data.

claim: Insertion of excised transposon termini places fAc and fAc-flanking DNA ahead of replication fork β and Ac and Ac-flanking DNA ahead of replication fork α to generate a rolling circle replicon.
source: Insertion of the excised transposon termini places fAc and fAc-flanking DNA ahead of replication fork β (upper chromatid), and Ac and Ac-flanking DNA ahead of replication fork α to generate a rolling circle replicon (lower chromatid).
evidence: This is part of the proposed model shown in Figure 1.

claim: Following re-replication of fAc, Ac, and a portion of the flanking sequences, DNA replication forks α and β stall and abort, resulting in chromatids terminated by broken ends.
source: Following re-replication of fAc, Ac, and a portion of the flanking sequences, DNA replication forks α and β stall and abort, resulting in chromatids terminated by broken ends (the red > or < symbol) (Michel et al., 1997).
evidence: This is part of the proposed model with citation support.

claim: Chromatid fusion produces a chromosome with two unequal sister chromatids: one containing a deletion and one containing a TDD and a CI.
source: Chromatid fusion produces a chromosome with two unequal sister chromatids: The upper chromatid contains a deletion of the segment from fAc to the a/b target site. The lower chromatid contains a TDD (left-hand loop), as well as a new CI (right-hand loop).
evidence: This is part of the proposed model shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Both TDD and TDDCI alleles contain similar duplication structures and should exhibit similar phenotypes.
source: Both TDD and TDDCI alleles contain similar duplication structures and should exhibit similar phenotypes.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the structural similarities.

claim: 25 candidate alleles were identified by screening maize ears.
source: We identified 25 candidate alleles, and cloned and sequenced the duplication/Ac junctions (the green segment flanking the Ac 5′ end in Figure 1E and Figure 2A) from 16 of the 25 TDD/TDDCI candidates via Ac casting (Singh et al., 2003; Wang and Peterson, 2013) or inverse PCR (iPCR) (See Zhang et al. (2013) for detailed screening and cloning methods).
evidence: This is experimental data from the study.

claim: Duplication/Ac junctions were cloned and sequenced from 16 of the 25 TDD/TDDCI candidates.
source: We identified 25 candidate alleles, and cloned and sequenced the duplication/Ac junctions (the green segment flanking the Ac 5′ end in Figure 1E and Figure 2A) from 16 of the 25 TDD/TDDCI candidates via Ac casting (Singh et al., 2003; Wang and Peterson, 2013) or inverse PCR (iPCR) (See Zhang et al. (2013) for detailed screening and cloning methods).
evidence: This is experimental data from the study.

claim: Primers 1 + Ac5 can amplify a product from both TDD and TDDCI alleles.
source: Primers 1 + Ac5 can amplify a product from both TDD and TDDCI while primers 2 + Ac3 can amplify a product only from TDDCI since the latter contains an additional CI (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is based on the primer design and allele structures shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Primers 2 + Ac3 can amplify a product only from TDDCI alleles since the latter contains an additional CI.
source: Primers 1 + Ac5 can amplify a product from both TDD and TDDCI while primers 2 + Ac3 can amplify a product only from TDDCI since the latter contains an additional CI (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is based on the primer design and allele structures shown in Figure 2A.

claim: PCR using primers 1 + Ac5 produced bands of the expected sizes in all 16 alleles tested.
source: As expected, PCR using primers 1 + Ac5 produced bands of the expected sizes in all the 16 alleles (Figure 2B, upper panel; seven examples are shown here).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Primers 2 + Ac3 produced bands with expected sizes from only seven alleles.
source: Whereas, primers 2 + Ac3 produced bands with expected sizes from only seven alleles (Figure 2B, lower panel).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Seven TDDCI candidates have duplication/insertion breakpoints located from 13,392 bp to 1.7 Mb proximal to the p1 locus on chromosome 1.
source: Sequencing of the PCR products obtained from primers 1 + Ac5 and 2 + Ac3 revealed that these seven TDDCI candidates have duplication/insertion breakpoints located from 13,392 bp to 1.7 Mb proximal to the p1 locus on chromosome 1 (Table 1).
evidence: This is experimental data from sequencing, shown in Table 1.

claim: The Ac termini in TDDCI alleles are flanked by 8-bp target site duplications (TSDs) as predicted by the model.
source: Importantly, the Ac termini are flanked by 8-bp target site duplications (TSDs; green/black triangles in Figure 1E) as predicted by the model in Figure 1 (See Supplementary file 1 for sequences containing TSDs).
evidence: This is experimental data that confirms the model prediction.

claim: Three red/white twinned sectors were identified, each consisting of a red kernel pericarp sector twinned with an adjacent white pericarp sector.
source: Of particular importance are the results derived from three red/white twinned sectors, in which a sector of red kernel pericarp (seed coat) is twinned with an adjacent white pericarp sector (Figure 3).
evidence: This is observational data shown in Figure 3.

claim: P1-rr alleles were isolated from each red pericarp sector and corresponding p1-ww alleles were isolated from each white twin sector.
source: From each red pericarp sector, we isolated P1-rr alleles (P1-rr-T21, P1-rr-T22 and P1-rr-T24), and from each white twin sector, we isolated corresponding p1-ww alleles (p1-ww-T21, p1-ww-T22, and p1-ww-T24).
evidence: This is experimental data from the study.

claim: Similar types of twinned pericarp sectors have been shown to arise from the reciprocal products of standard Ac transposition events.
source: Similar types of twinned pericarp sectors have been shown to arise from the reciprocal products of standard Ac transposition events (Greenblatt and Brink, 1962; Chen et al., 1992).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Each pair of red/white twinned alleles are derived from the reciprocal TDDCI/deletion products of RET.
source: Here, we propose that each pair of red/white twinned alleles are derived from the reciprocal TDDCI/deletion products of RET (sister chromatids shown in Figure 1E).
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the observed data.

claim: For each pair of red/white co-twins, the sequences of the PCR products obtained using primers 2 + Ac3 are identical.
source: Moreover, for each pair of red/white co-twins, the sequences of the PCR products obtained using primers 2 + Ac3 are identical (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is experimental data from sequencing.

claim: The results are consistent with the model of RET during DNA replication as shown in Figure 1.
source: Together these results are consistent with the model of RET during DNA replication as shown in Figure 1.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data.

claim: The 12.7 kb p1 band is absent in the three twinned p1-ww alleles.
source: First, the 12.7 kb p1 band is absent in the three twinned p1-ww alleles (p1-ww-T22, p1-ww-T24, and p1-ww-T21; Figure 2C, lanes 4, 6 and 10, respectively).
evidence: This is experimental data from DNA gel blot analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The absence of the 12.7 kb p1 band in p1-ww alleles confirms the presence of a deletion as predicted by the model.
source: This result confirms the presence of a deletion as predicted by the model shown in Figure 1.
evidence: This is an inference from the gel blot data that supports the model.

claim: The alleles P1-rr-T24, P1-rr-E17, and P1-rr-E340 show a more intense 4.7 kb p2 band in comparison with the 5.0 kb band.
source: Second, the alleles P1-rr-T24, P1-rr-E17, and P1-rr-E340 show a more intense 4.7 kb p2 band in comparison with the 5.0 kb band (Figure 2C, lanes 5, 7, 8).
evidence: This is experimental data from DNA gel blot analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The more intense 4.7 kb p2 band in P1-rr-T24, P1-rr-E17, and P1-rr-E340 is expected because these three alleles have duplications of >70 kb that generate additional copies of the p2 gene.
source: This result is also expected because these three alleles have duplications of >70 kb (Table 1) that generate additional copies of the p2 gene located ∼70 kb proximal to p1.
evidence: This is an inference from the gel blot data and duplication sizes.

claim: Alleles P1-rr-T22, P1-rr-T21, and P1-rr-E5 exhibit one or two new bands hybridizing with probe 8B.
source: Third, alleles P1-rr-T22, P1-rr-T21, and P1-rr-E5 (Figure 2C, lanes 3, 9 and 12, respectively) exhibit one or two new bands hybridizing with probe 8B.
evidence: This is experimental data from DNA gel blot analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The new bands hybridizing with probe 8B in P1-rr-T22, P1-rr-T21, and P1-rr-E5 are consistent with the presence of a CI that contains a newly-generated copy of the 8B sequence.
source: This is consistent with the presence of a CI that contains a newly-generated copy of the 8B sequence (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is an inference from the gel blot data.

claim: In P1-rr-T22, the duplication/insertion breakpoint occurred in the p2 band containing probe 8B, resulting in a shift of the 4.7 kb band to ∼8 kb.
source: In P1-rr-T22, the duplication/insertion breakpoint occurred in the p2 band containing probe 8B, resulting in a shift of the 4.7 kb band to ∼8 kb (Figure 2C, lane 3).
evidence: This is an inference from the gel blot data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The ∼8 kb band in P1-rr-T22 is more intense than the 5.0 kb p1-ww[4Co63] band and the 12.7 kb p1 band.
source: Moreover, this ∼8 kb band is more intense than the 5.0 kb p1-ww[4Co63] band and the 12.7 kb p1 band in P1-rr-T22 (lane 3 in Figure 2C).
evidence: This is experimental data from DNA gel blot analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The intense ∼8 kb band in P1-rr-T22 is actually a triplet containing two copies of a new 8461 bp p1 fragment (one from the TDD, and a second from the CI) and one copy of a 8127 bp p2 fragment from the rearrangement junction.
source: The model in Figure 1 and our analyses indicate that the intense ∼8 kb band is actually a triplet containing two copies of a new 8461 bp p1 fragment (one from the TDD, and a second from the CI, see below) and one copy of a 8127 bp p2 fragment from the rearrangement junction.
evidence: This is an inference from the model and gel blot data.

claim: Further DNA gel blot analyses with a different p1 probe confirm that P1-rr-T22 contains a TDD.
source: Further DNA gel blot analyses with a different p1 probe (not shown) confirm that P1-rr-T22 contains a TDD.
evidence: This is experimental data from additional gel blot analysis.

claim: The four alleles P1-rr-T22, P1-rr-T24, P1-rr-E17, and P1-rr-E340 contain the TDDCI structure.
source: All together, these results indicate that these four alleles—P1-rr-T22, P1-rr-T24, P1-rr-E17, and P1-rr-E340—contain the TDDCI structure.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental results.

claim: The model predicts that the insertion size and structure are determined by where re-replication aborts and how the resulting DSBs are repaired.
source: The model in Figure 1 predicts that the insertion size and structure are determined by where re-replication aborts and how the resulting DSBs are repaired (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is part of the proposed model shown in Figure 1.

claim: The CI in P1-rr-T22 is 23,238 bp in length, consisting of 14,484 bp of fAc and its distal flanking sequence and 8754 bp of Ac and its proximal flanking sequence.
source: The CI in P1-rr-T22 is 23,238 bp in length (GenBank accession # KM013690), consisting of 14,484 bp of fAc and its distal flanking sequence and 8754 bp of Ac and its proximal flanking sequence (Figure 4); these two fragments are joined at a 4-bp microhomology sequence consistent with DSB repair via non-homologous end joining (NHEJ).
evidence: This is experimental data from sequencing.

claim: The two fragments in the CI of P1-rr-T22 are joined at a 4-bp microhomology sequence consistent with DSB repair via non-homologous end joining (NHEJ).
source: The CI in P1-rr-T22 is 23,238 bp in length (GenBank accession # KM013690), consisting of 14,484 bp of fAc and its distal flanking sequence and 8754 bp of Ac and its proximal flanking sequence (Figure 4); these two fragments are joined at a 4-bp microhomology sequence consistent with DSB repair via non-homologous end joining (NHEJ).
evidence: This is inferred from the sequence data.

claim: The P1-rr-T22 allele carries a 70-kb TDD.
source: In addition to the CI, the P1-rr-T22 allele carries a 70-kb TDD (Table 1), and its white co-twin p1-ww-T22 carries a reciprocal 70-kb deletion; moreover, the breakpoints of both the P1-rr-T22 duplication and p1-ww-T22 deletion contain 8-bp target site duplications.
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Table 1.

claim: The white co-twin p1-ww-T22 carries a reciprocal 70-kb deletion.
source: In addition to the CI, the P1-rr-T22 allele carries a 70-kb TDD (Table 1), and its white co-twin p1-ww-T22 carries a reciprocal 70-kb deletion; moreover, the breakpoints of both the P1-rr-T22 duplication and p1-ww-T22 deletion contain 8-bp target site duplications.
evidence: This is experimental data.

claim: The breakpoints of both the P1-rr-T22 duplication and p1-ww-T22 deletion contain 8-bp target site duplications.
source: In addition to the CI, the P1-rr-T22 allele carries a 70-kb TDD (Table 1), and its white co-twin p1-ww-T22 carries a reciprocal 70-kb deletion; moreover, the breakpoints of both the P1-rr-T22 duplication and p1-ww-T22 deletion contain 8-bp target site duplications.
evidence: This is experimental data from sequencing.

claim: All features of P1-rr-T22 and p1-ww-T22 are predicted by the RET/re-replication model shown in Figure 1.
source: All of these features are predicted by the RET/re-replication model shown in Figure 1.
evidence: This is an inference that the data supports the model.

claim: The CI in P1-rr-E17 is 19,341 bp in length.
source: The CI in P1-rr-E17 (GenBank accession # KM013689) is 19,341 bp in length (Figure 4); its structure suggests that the DSBs predicted in Figure 1D were repaired via homologous recombination (HR) between two direct repeat sequences that flank the p1 gene in P1-ovov454 (Lechelt et al., 1989).
evidence: This is experimental data from sequencing.

claim: The structure of the CI in P1-rr-E17 suggests that the DSBs were repaired via homologous recombination (HR) between two direct repeat sequences that flank the p1 gene in P1-ovov454.
source: The CI in P1-rr-E17 (GenBank accession # KM013689) is 19,341 bp in length (Figure 4); its structure suggests that the DSBs predicted in Figure 1D were repaired via homologous recombination (HR) between two direct repeat sequences that flank the p1 gene in P1-ovov454 (Lechelt et al., 1989).
evidence: This is inferred from the sequence structure and cited prior research.

claim: Two direct repeat sequences flank the p1 gene in P1-ovov454.
source: The CI in P1-rr-E17 (GenBank accession # KM013689) is 19,341 bp in length (Figure 4); its structure suggests that the DSBs predicted in Figure 1D were repaired via homologous recombination (HR) between two direct repeat sequences that flank the p1 gene in P1-ovov454 (Lechelt et al., 1989).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: The p1-flanking repeats are 5248 bp in length.
source: These repeats (hatched boxes in Figure 2A) are 5248 bp in length; the proximal copy is 4555 bp from the Ac element while the distal copy is 2934 bp from fAc (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is structural information shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The proximal copy of the p1-flanking repeat is 4555 bp from the Ac element while the distal copy is 2934 bp from fAc.
source: These repeats (hatched boxes in Figure 2A) are 5248 bp in length; the proximal copy is 4555 bp from the Ac element while the distal copy is 2934 bp from fAc (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is structural information shown in Figure 2A.

claim: If re-replication continued beyond the Ac and fAc segments and into the flanking 5248 bp repeats before aborting, then the DSBs could be repaired via HR to generate the observed structures.
source: If re-replication continued beyond the Ac and fAc segments and into the flanking 5248 bp repeats before aborting, then the DSBs could be repaired via HR to generate the observed structures (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism to explain the observed structure.

claim: The two repeat copies flanking P1-ovov454 differ at six SNPs in the distal half of the repeats.
source: The two repeat copies flanking P1-ovov454 differ at six SNPs in the distal half of the repeats (Figure 2A, red vertical short lines in the hatched box).
evidence: This is sequence data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Sequences of the P1-rr-E17 allele show that the repeat in the CI is identical to the proximal copy.
source: Sequences of the P1-rr-E17 allele show that the repeat in the CI is identical to the proximal copy.
evidence: This is experimental data from sequencing.

claim: The results suggest that the HR crossover in P1-rr-E17 occurred between the proximal halves of the two repeats.
source: These results suggest that the HR crossover occurred between the proximal halves of the two repeats (Figure 5).
evidence: This is inferred from the sequence data.

claim: For P1-rr-T24, no product could be amplified using the divergent primer strategy.
source: For P1-rr-T24, no product could be amplified using the divergent primer strategy described above.
evidence: This is experimental data from PCR.

claim: A band of ∼5.0 kb could be amplified from P1-rr-T24 using primers 1 + 2 which flank the insertion site.
source: However, a band of ∼5.0 kb could be amplified using primers 1 + 2 which flank the insertion site.
evidence: This is experimental data from PCR.

claim: The ∼5.0 kb band from P1-rr-T24 was sequenced and found to contain an intact Ac element.
source: This band was sequenced and found to contain an intact Ac element (Figure 4).
evidence: This is experimental data from sequencing.

claim: It is very unlikely that the Ac in P1-rr-T24 was inserted through a simple transposition event, because the insertion site is located precisely at the duplication junction that is generated by RET.
source: It seems very unlikely that this Ac was inserted through a simple transposition event, because the insertion site is located precisely at the duplication junction that is generated by RET, and an independent Ac transposition would not be expected to insert into precisely the same site.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the improbability of the coincidence.

claim: The Ac insertion in P1-rr-T24 was produced by HR between the re-replicated Ac and fAc segments as they share 2039 bp of sequence identity.
source: We suggest that the Ac insertion in P1-rr-T24 was produced by HR between the re-replicated Ac and fAc segments as they share 2039 bp of sequence identity (Figure 6 and Video 2).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on sequence homology.

claim: The structure of the CI in P1-rr-E340 is still unknown.
source: Finally, the structure of the CI in P1-rr-E340 is still unknown; DNA gel blotting (not shown) indicated that the Ac-proximal fragment is in the range of 18–90 kb and the fAc-distal fragment is greater than 18 kb, resulting in a CI of at least 36 kb in length.
evidence: This is stated explicitly in the text.

claim: DNA gel blotting indicated that the Ac-proximal fragment in P1-rr-E340 is in the range of 18–90 kb and the fAc-distal fragment is greater than 18 kb, resulting in a CI of at least 36 kb in length.
source: Finally, the structure of the CI in P1-rr-E340 is still unknown; DNA gel blotting (not shown) indicated that the Ac-proximal fragment is in the range of 18–90 kb and the fAc-distal fragment is greater than 18 kb, resulting in a CI of at least 36 kb in length.
evidence: This is experimental data from DNA gel blotting.

claim: PCR results show that the P1-rr-E311, P1-rr-T21, and P1-rr-E5 alleles contain junctions consistent with the presence of CI.
source: PCR results show that the P1-rr-E311, P1-rr-T21, and P1-rr-E5 alleles contain junctions consistent with the presence of CI (Figure 2B, lanes 12–18).
